threat: Phishing harvests a CRC/site credential; attacker impersonates a legitimate site user to enter/alter eCRF
rationale: Phishing of site users is common; grants entry to eCRF data

threat: eCRF data / e-signatures altered in transit if TLS is weak or misconfigured
rationale: TLS 1.2+ is assumed; in-transit tampering requires defeating it

threat: Web-app flaw (broken access control / injection) lets a user act beyond their role
rationale: Validated commercial EDC; app-layer flaws possible but not routine

threat: CRO user's credential phished; attacker logs in as a valid CRO account
impact: Full delegated access under a trusted identity
rationale: CRO credential phishing is common; a valid account opens the environment

threat: Over-broad or stale CRO delegated account reaches data/functions beyond remit
impact: Excess, unmonitored exposure of trial data
rationale: Over-broad / stale third-party access is a recurring real-world weakness
recText: Least privilege with periodic entitlement recertification

threat: Change made under a valid CRO identity; audit attributes it to a legitimate user, so malice can't be proven
rationale: Change under a valid identity → integrity indefensible at inspection
recText: Behavioural anomaly monitoring over the audit trail

threat: IdP compromise or token forgery enables environment-wide impersonation
rationale: IdP compromise is hard but gives systemic impersonation

threat: Misconfigured RBAC or auth flaw allows privilege escalation
impact: Rights to alter data the user shouldn't
rationale: RBAC misconfiguration is a realistic, recurring operational error
recText: Least privilege with periodic entitlement recertification

threat: Session token replay / forgery to hijack a valid session
rationale: Token replay needs interception; mitigated by session controls

threat: Direct database-layer modification of CRF values, bypassing the application and its audit trail
impact: Silent integrity breach, no audit record
rationale: DB-layer tampering needs privileged access but bypasses the audit trail

threat: Change made with valid credentials is recorded as authorised; attacker cannot be distinguished from a legitimate user
impact: Integrity guarantee defeated; ALCOA+ Attributable broken
rationale: Valid-credential change recorded as authorised: the core blind spot
recText: Behavioural anomaly monitoring over the audit trail

threat: Bulk read/query of subject PII/PHI from the repository
rationale: PII/PHI breach; regulatory + reputational

threat: Attacker with admin access alters/deletes audit logs to erase evidence
impact: Loss of the record used to prove integrity
rationale: Needs admin, but destroys the very evidence integrity is proven with

threat: Monitoring disabled or flooded to evade detection
rationale: Disabling monitoring is an enabler, not a direct data harm

threat: Source data injected or altered at ingestion
impact: Corrupted source data enters the record
rationale: Requires compromising a feed, but injects corrupt data at source

threat: Spoofed integration endpoint feeds false data into the EDC
rationale: Endpoint authentication assumed; spoofing a vendor feed is non-trivial

threat: Unvalidated message/file processing corrupts or injects records
impact: Integrity compromise at the integration layer
rationale: Validation exists at the integration layer, but is imperfect

threat: Unmonitored bulk export of datasets / PII out of the environment
rationale: Bulk export is a routine function; monitoring of it is often absent

threat: Malicious or erroneous reconciliation alters CRF values under a valid DM identity
impact: Integrity breach masked as routine cleaning
rationale: Reconciliation write-back is a routine path to alter data under valid access
recText: Behavioural anomaly monitoring over the audit trail

threat: Manipulated derivation logic changes SDTM/ADaM/TLF outputs
rationale: Requires programming access, but corrupts the analysis datasets

threat: Submission package altered before or during submission
rationale: Tampering the submission package directly corrupts regulatory data
recText: Cryptographic integrity seal across freeze → submission

threat: No integrity proof that the submitted dataset matches the source of truth
rationale: Absence of an integrity proof is a standing condition, not a rare event
recText: Cryptographic integrity seal across freeze → submission

threat: Backup exfiltration if keys/access are compromised
rationale: Backups encrypted at rest; exposure needs key/access compromise

threat: Malicious restore of manipulated data / ransomware impact
impact: Integrity or availability compromise near lock
rationale: Recoverable in most cases; severity spikes near database lock

threat: Unauthorised access to treatment-allocation / randomisation data causes unblinding of the study
impact: Trial validity compromised; bias introduced into results
rationale: Access to allocation data is restricted, but unblinding destroys trial validity
recText: Monitor access to randomisation / allocation data

threat: Version confusion / loss of lineage between working, derived and source datasets allows an incorrect or substituted dataset to be used undetected
impact: Wrong dataset analysed or submitted; derivation cannot be traced
rationale: Version/lineage confusion is a realistic operational failure with submission-level consequences

threat: Reconciliation failure: missing or duplicated records from external feeds go undetected
rationale: Reconciliation gaps are common; produce incomplete or duplicated records

threat: Retention failure: records deleted, backups unrestorable, or retention period not met
impact: Records unavailable at inspection; regulatory non-compliance
rationale: Retention controls usually exist; failure surfaces only at inspection

threat: Wrong-version dataset frozen or submitted, or approval evidence missing at the freeze point
impact: Regulator receives a superseded or unapproved version
rationale: Freezing or submitting the wrong version directly corrupts the regulatory record
recText: Cryptographic integrity seal across freeze → submission
